compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (Blackwell): plenty of tensor-core throughput at fp16; small inner C=32 limits tensor-core utilization for attention QK/AV matmuls (16x16x32). Linear layers fc1 (32->128) and fc2 (128->32) are GEMV-like at per-token granularity but can be tiled by token blocks.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Block: B=1, H=720, W=1280, C=32, window 4x4 (N=16), heads=1, mlp_ratio=4 -> hidden=128. Tokens total = 921600. Windows = 57600. Attention per window is tiny (16x16x32). Bandwidth-bound overall.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Small C may underutilize tensor cores; fusion is the main lever.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Activation tensor is 921600 x 32 fp16 = ~56 MB; reading/writing this multiple times across LN/QKV/attn/proj/LN/FC1/GELU/FC2 dominates. Weights are tiny (qkv 32x96, proj 32x32, fc1 32x128, fc2 128x32) and fit easily in shared/registers.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Multiple global round-trips in baseline; fusion can drastically reduce DRAM traffic.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window working set: N=16 tokens x C=32 fp16 (=1KB) plus hidden 128 (=4KB). Q,K,V,attn(16x16), softmax workspace easily fit per-CTA in shared. Weights: qkv 6KB, proj 2KB, fc1 8KB, fc2 8KB -> ~24KB shared/constant per CTA, very tractable.
register_pressure.risk: If fully fused per-window, register usage for fc1 hidden (128) per token may be high; can iterate over tokens.

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused transformer block (LayerNorm + windowed self-attention (1 head, window 4x4) + residual + LayerNorm + MLP(32->128->32 GELU) + residual). Reductions: LN mean/var, softmax. Dense, no shifts. 2) Canonical: y1 = x + Proj(Softmax(Q*K^T/sqrt(C)+RPE) V) where Q,K,V from Linear(LN(x)); y2 = y1 + FC2(GELU(FC1(LN(y1)))). 3) Shapes: x (1,720,1280,32) fp16. Window (4,4) -> N=16 tokens per window. nH=180,nW=320 -> 57600 windows. Weights tiny. 4) Regimes: (a) Attention path is bandwidth-bound (small C, tiny GEMMs), (b) MLP path bandwidth-bound (hidden=128 small), (c) LN reductions trivial; overall DRAM traffic dominates. 5) Knobs: fuse entire block per window CTA; cache weights in shared; vectorize loads (fp16x2); use tl.dot for 16x16x32 matmuls; tile multiple windows per CTA to amortize weight loads; choose between two kernels (attn-fused, mlp-fused) vs single mega-kernel. 6) Skeleton: per-CTA load WINDOWS_PER_CTA windows of N x C; compute LN1; QKV via tl.dot with weight tile in shared; compute attn 16x16 + RPE + softmax; AV; proj; add residual; LN2; FC1 (16xC) x (Cxhidden); GELU; FC2; add residual; store. 7) Families considered: (A) Single mega-kernel fusing whole block per window-group [TOP - working set fits], (B) Two fused kernels split at residual2 (attn-fused, mlp-fused), (C) Per-op Triton kernels matching torch.compile (baseline). Family A preferred since weights total ~24KB easily fit in SMEM and intermediates fit in regs. RPE bias (16x16 fp16 = 512B) loaded once per CTA from constant. Need to be careful with LN fp32 accumulation for numerical match.

action.description: Single Triton kernel that, per CTA, processes one or a small group of 4x4 windows end-to-end: LN1 -> QKV (tl.dot with weights in shared) -> attn(16x16)+RPE+softmax -> AV -> Proj+residual -> LN2 -> FC1(32->128) -> GELU -> FC2(128->32) -> residual -> store. All weights cached in shared memory (qkv 32x96, proj 32x32, fc1 32x128, fc2 128x32). Use fp32 accumulators for LN mean/var and matmul accum; fp16 storage. Use tl.dot for the matmuls; window is 16 tokens x 32 channels (perfect 16x16x32 tensor-core tile).
action.rationale: Eliminates ~6-8 DRAM round-trips of the 56MB activation tensor. Working set per CTA is small enough to fit, and the 16x16x32 tile maps cleanly onto Blackwell tensor cores.
action.title: Mega-fused per-window Swin block kernel

action.description: Two fused Triton kernels: (1) LN1 + QKV + attention(softmax+RPE) + AV + Proj + residual1, writing y1 to global; (2) LN2 + FC1 + GELU + FC2 + residual2. Each kernel keeps its respective weights in shared. Simpler than mega-fusion; one extra round-trip of y1 vs n1.

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin block in fp16 on input (1,720,1280,32): LN -> windowed self-attention (window 4x4, single head, no shift, with relative-position bias) -> residual -> LN -> MLP(32->128 GELU ->32) -> residual. Each window has only N=16 tokens and C=32 channels; all weights are tiny (qkv 32x96, proj 32x32, fc1 32x128, fc2 128x32 ≈ 24KB total fp16). The workload is strongly DRAM-bandwidth-bound: the ~56MB activation tensor would otherwise be streamed through DRAM many times across the op sequence. Key constraints: fp16 storage with fp32 accumulation for LN/softmax/matmul for numerical parity; 57600 windows; tensor-core-friendly 16x16x32 tiles; RPE is a fixed 16x16 fp16 broadcast bias.
open_questions: Exact tolerance required vs reference (LN/softmax fp32 accumulation must match torch.compile output within ~1e-2 fp16)?
Is the input always contiguous (B,H,W,C) with H,W divisible by 4 at benchmark time?
Best WINDOWS_PER_CTA on RTX5090 (1, 2, or 4) given register budget for hidden 16*WPC x 128 fp32 accumulator?
Should weights be preloaded once via tl.load into shared per CTA, or kept as constants/inline arguments?
Will Triton's tl.dot accept M=16 tiles efficiently on Blackwell, or does it require padding M to 32?
Does the RPE bias need to be reshaped/transposed for efficient broadcast inside the kernel?
Is there benefit to converting fc1/fc2 weights to a packed/transposed layout at __init__ time for better tl.dot operand layout?
How much does torch.compile already fuse here, i.e., what is the realistic speedup ceiling?
